title: Helping people help themselves: A modularized and online-based self-help intervention for people with psychological distress in mecklenburg-western pomerania (eHelp-MV)
summary:
The overarching project goals of eHelp-MV are to use a low-threshold, digital self-help intervention:
(1) to provide rapid help to those suffering from mental distress, 
(2) to counteract an increase in mental disorders and (3) to minimize the overburdening of the existing psychotherapeutic and psychiatric care system. 

To this end, this study will examine the effectiveness, psychometric evaluation and implementation of the four eHelp-MV self-help interventions for reducing general symptom severity, increasing module-specific knowledge and examining cost-effectiveness using a progress measurement at four points in time.
conditions: general psychological distress and symptom severity measured by: PHQ-9, MEDI, BSI.

interventions.name:
Randomized allocation of subjects to the preference condition. Selection of the intervention arm 1 or 2 in dependency of subject preference. 
Intervention arm 1 comprises the participation in two sucessively four-week digital self-help interventions: "Being Mindful" and "Thinking Flexibly".

Randomized allocation of subjects to the randomization condition. Randomized allocation to intervention arm 1 or 2. 
Intervention arm 2 comprises the participation in the two sucessively four-week digital self-help intervention: "Improving Interpersonal Problems" and "Promoting Wellbeing".

Randomized allocation of subjects to the control condition, which corresponds to a naturalistic control group consisting of waiting list patients of the Centre for Psychological Psychotherapy Greifswald. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Waiting list patients of the ZPP Greifswald, for whom the indication for outpatient psychotherapy was given after a psychotherapeutic consultation and detailed initial diagnostics.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria are defined as acute danger to self and others, acute psychotic experiences and parallel (partial) inpatient or outpatient psychotherapeutic treatment.
